newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks push ahead in early morning.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks push ahead in early morning.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks advanced in early Monday morning trade, rebounding from last week's depressed territory and despite weakness in other markets, brokers said.
"The index was extremely oversold last week. This is a technical rebound," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Centuries Securities.
The Hang Seng Index was trading 107 points higher at 12,596 on heavy turnover HK$1.59 billion. Property stocks led the market from the open.
"These stocks were also deeply oversold last week," said Shum.
Sun Hung Kai Properties led the sector putting on HK$2.25 to HK$84.50 and Henderson Land put on HK$1.50 to HK$65.50.
Analysts said they did not believe the companies' recently released 1996 results or the upcoming government land auction on Wednesday were boosting sentiment and prices.
The commercial and industrial sector followed, led by Swire Pacific with a gain of HK$1.75 to HK$60.25. CITIC Pacific added HK$0.60 to HK$38.60.
"It is highly possible that we will see an increase in interest rates tomorrow night, but this has been totally discounted," said Lino Delgado, associate director of Amsteel Securities.
The sites to be auctioned at the government land auction are good well located lots and should attract good interest, said Delgado.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings advanced only HK$0.50 to HK$177.00.
Hang Seng Index futures also rebounded, although trading was not active.Hang Seng Index futures also rebounded, although trading was not active.
"Most investors are rolling over their contracts to the next month," said Kenneth Tang, director of Sassoon Futures. "Futures are not leading this market."
The March contract was trading 175 points higher at 12,625 and still at a sizeable discount to the buoyant cash market.
